draft.title: Energy flow in an ecosystem
card: Nearly all the energy in an ecosystem comes from sunlight. Producers capture some of it and store it as chemical energy in their food.
Energy passes to the next feeding level when one organism eats another. A consumer gets only the energy stored in the food it eats.
At each step, much of the energy is lost to the surroundings as heat. Organisms use energy to move, grow and stay alive, and this releases heat.
Less energy reaches each higher feeding level, so it can support fewer organisms. This is why there are fewer top consumers than producers.
draft.remember: Energy flows one way and shrinks at each step, so higher levels have fewer organisms.

a.q: Why are there fewer hawks than mice in a grassland?
opts: Less energy reaches each higher feeding level
Hawks make less energy from sunlight than mice
Energy passes back down from hawks to mice
Mice use up all the energy in the grass they eat
a.why: Much energy is lost as heat at each step, so less is left for the hawks, which supports fewer of them. Hawks do not make energy from sunlight, because only producers capture it.
a.clue: Think about what happens to energy at each step.

b.q: In a pond, algae are eaten by water fleas, which are eaten by small fish, which are eaten by a heron. Which feeding level gets the least energy from the algae?
opts: The heron
The small fish
The water fleas
The algae
b.why: Energy is lost as heat at each step, so the heron, at the end of the chain, receives the least. The algae capture energy from the sunlight themselves, so they do not get it from the algae.
b.clue: Count the steps from the producer to each level.

a.best: Less energy reaches each higher feeding level

problems.detail: 'Which feeding level gets the least energy from the algae?' can be read literally so that the algae get none from themselves, which makes 'The algae' a tempting trick answer. The why has to argue this away. Reword, e.g. 'Which organism receives the least of the energy the algae captured?' or 'Which consumer gets the least energy?'

'Energy flows one way' is not stated on the card. Also, 'shrinks' could suggest energy disappears, while the card says it is lost to the surroundings as heat. Consider 'less energy passes on at each step'.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both questions have one clear answer. Question b's wording 'energy from the algae' lets 'The algae' be read as getting none, and the remember line adds 'flows one way', which the card does not teach.
